# The apex guide links into trees the split moved, and no check can see it

> ## 🔴 PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-08-30 — the original Problem section below is DISPROVEN
>
> **This ticket was filed on a measurement error, and it closes on its second finding instead.** The correction is in the body rather than only in a comment because merge freezes the body as the permanent record.
>
> `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` has **zero** dead relative links, at every ref including `915c1a01e7` — the one this ticket measures at:
>
> | ref | total | relative | dead |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `21da68021a` (pre-cut) | 14 | 14 | 0 |
> | `c623b2f63c` (the cut) | 15 | 5 | 0 |
> | `915c1a01e7` (this ticket's ref) | 15 | 5 | 0 |
> | `origin/dev` | 15 | 5 | 0 |
>
> **`c623b2f63c` repointed 8 links from relative to absolute `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` URLs in the same commit that removed the trees** — `git show` on that file reports exactly 8 insertions and 8 deletions. The repointing and the removal were atomic, so nothing was ever orphaned.
>
> ⭐ **The error, stated exactly because the shape recurs:** the *"14 relative links"* figure is the file's inventory **before** the cut. I enumerated links from one revision and resolved them against another revision's tree. Every individual `git cat-file -e` was correct; the link set they were run against belonged to a different commit. A resolver cannot detect that — it answers faithfully about whatever it is handed.
>
> ⭐ **And the inference underneath it:** I reasoned that removing a tree must leave its inbound links dead. True in general, false here, because whoever executed the cut handled it in the same commit. **I inferred the consequence of an action instead of measuring its result.**
>
> **The ticket's second finding carries it, and carries it further.** There was no link checker — confirmed. The real population is **11 dead links across 9 files, none in `Introduction.md`**, and none of them split fallout: relative-depth authoring mistakes and stale portal ids. That makes the guard **more** necessary, not less — ordinary authoring is the hazard, and no custody decision would have prevented any of them.
>
> **AC-1 and AC-2 were satisfied before this ticket existed** — not fixed by it. AC-3/4/5 are delivered by PR #17859. Full restatement, Contract Ledger rows and the 11 repoints: [comment 5464382349](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17809#issuecomment-5464382349) by @neo-opus-ada, who declined to edit a foreign-authored premise and asked the author instead — the correct boundary, held at the cost of two hours that were mine. Ruling: [comment 5465202069](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17809#issuecomment-5465202069).
>
> **Everything below this line is the original filing, retained unedited as the specimen.** It is wrong about the cause and right that the file class needed a guard.

---

## Context

`learn/benefits/Introduction.md` is the Engine's apex identity document — [#17808](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17808) names it *"canonical"* and derives the README's framing from it. After the Agent OS cut ([PR #17806](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/17806), merged as `c623b2f63c`), **8 of its 14 relative links resolve to nothing on `dev`.**

Measured at `origin/dev` `915c1a01e7` by resolving every relative link with `git cat-file -e`, not by reading a working tree — a local checkout still carrying the pre-cut trees reports all 14 healthy, which is how this stayed invisible.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open Engine issues at 2026-08-27T08:56Z; no equivalent ticket. A2A in-flight sweep: latest 30 messages across read states — active claims are `neo-agent-institution#1/#2/#3` and `#17807`/`#17808`/`neo-agent-brain#181`/`#182`; none claims `learn/benefits`.

## The Problem

| broken target | class |
|---|---|
| `learn/agentos/DreamPipeline.md` | Agent OS guide, moved to the Brain |
| `learn/agentos/MX.md` | ” |
| `learn/agentos/MemoryCore.md` | ” |
| `learn/agentos/SwarmIntelligence.md` | ” |
| `learn/benefits/brain/AIEngineeringTeam.md` | Brain benefits guide, moved |
| `learn/benefits/brain/AgentOSOnYourCodebase.md` | ” |
| `learn/benefits/brain/DeployingTheAgentOS.md` | ” |
| `learn/benefits/brain/IdentityRitualsCulture.md` | ” |

`learn/agentos/` went **137 → 26 tracked files**; the `learn/benefits/brain/` subdirectory left entirely. `learn/agentos/NeuralLink.md` survived, so this is not "the whole tree moved" — it is a partial move that a whole-directory assumption will get wrong.

**The damage is concentrated in the commercial half.** All four `brain/` links are the outbound doors from §8 *"What's in it for you"* — the section that carries the multi-tenant product story (*"you don't get Neo's team either… Teams adopt the working model"*). A reader who follows the pitch to its evidence gets four dead links. §4's "The Brain — where the institution lives" loses its four supporting guides the same way.

Custody was decided correctly and **publication silently followed it.** Those are two questions and only one was answered.

## The Architectural Reality

- ADR 0040 §5's custody table routes *"guides and decision records whose subject is the Body or the Engine"* to `neomjs/neo`, and Agent OS guides to the Brain. Both halves executed as designed; nothing here challenges that.
- What no rule covered: an Engine-owned document whose **links point at moved subjects**. Custody moved the target and left the referrer behind.
- [#17808](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17808) Fix item 4 already names this exact class — *"Replace stale filesystem-relative Brain doors with canonical sibling links where necessary"* — but bounds itself: *"This ticket changes the Engine README only."* The class is named; the population is larger and unowned.
- **No link checker exists.** `grep -rlE "link.?check|markdown.?link|dead.?link"` over `.github/workflows/` and `buildScripts/` returns zero, which is why 8 dead links merged without a red. Absence of a run is not a failure signal — the same shape [#17783](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17783) records as trigger starvation.

## The Fix

1. Repoint the 8 links to canonical sibling URLs on `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, following [#17808](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17808) Fix item 4's established pattern. Verify each target exists in the Brain before pointing at it — a link that 404s on a sibling is not an improvement over one that 404s locally.
2. Sweep the rest of `learn/benefits/**` with the same instrument; `Introduction.md` is where this was found, not necessarily where it ends.
3. Add a relative-link checker to `buildScripts/util/` (sibling precedent: the `check-*.mjs` family already invoked from `lint-staged` and `.husky/pre-push`) and wire it so a broken relative link under `learn/**` fails loud. It must resolve against the **committed tree**, not the working directory — a working-tree check is exactly the instrument that reported 14/14 healthy here.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` links | ADR 0040 §5 custody table; #17808 Fix item 4 | 8 relative links become canonical sibling URLs | Leave a link relative only when its target is still Engine-owned | the file itself | all 14 resolve at `origin/dev` via `git cat-file -e` |
| `buildScripts/util/` link checker | `check-*.mjs` family precedent | Non-zero exit naming each unresolved link and its referrer | none — the point is failing loud | script JSDoc | a mutation test: break one link, prove the checker reports it |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0040` — §5's custody table is correct and unchallenged. This ticket closes the referrer-side gap that custody-by-subject left open, and records that publication does not follow custody automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — every relative link in `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` resolves against `origin/dev`'s committed tree; the resolver output is pasted in the PR, and its instrument reads the tree rather than the working directory.
- [ ] **AC-2** — each of the 8 repointed targets is verified to exist in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` at a named ref, with the check shown.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the rest of `learn/benefits/**` is swept with the same instrument; the count of files checked and links resolved is reported, including a zero if the rest is clean.
- [ ] **AC-4** — a relative-link checker lands in `buildScripts/util/` and is wired into an enforcement surface that runs on `learn/**` changes.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the checker is proven able to fail: break one link deliberately, show it reported *that* link by name, restore. A green from a checker that has never gone red is not evidence.

## Out of Scope

- Re-deciding which guides moved — ADR 0040 §5 settled custody and this ticket does not reopen it.
- A publishing pipeline for the 111 `learn/agentos` files and 6 Brain benefit guides now in the Brain with no portal path. Real, separate, and Brain-side.
- The Engine README — [#17808](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17808) owns it.
- Absolute/external URL liveness. Relative-link integrity only; an external link checker is a different instrument with different failure modes.

## Avoided Traps

- **Directory-level assumption.** `learn/agentos/NeuralLink.md` survived while four siblings left. Any fix that rewrites `learn/agentos/*` wholesale will break the one link that is currently correct.
- **Checking the working tree.** The pre-cut checkout reports 14/14 healthy. A checker that resolves against the filesystem reproduces the blindness rather than removing it.
- **A checker that only logs.** #17730's lesson, recorded in [#17783](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17783)'s neighbourhood: a check whose result does not block is a log line.

## AC-1 / AC-2: the 8 links are not broken, at any ref

`learn/benefits/Introduction.md`, resolved against the **committed** tree:

| ref | total | relative | dead |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c623b2f63c~1` (pre-cut) | 14 | 14 | **0** |
| `c623b2f63c` (the cut) | 15 | 5 | **0** |
| `915c1a01e7` (this ticket's ref) | 15 | 5 | **0** |
| `origin/dev` | 15 | 5 | **0** |

The cut commit repointed those links to absolute `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` URLs **in the same commit** that removed the trees. All 8 named targets are present today as absolute URLs.

The `14 relative links` figure matches the file **before** the cut — so the reading looks like content from one ref resolved against targets at another. That is the hazard this ticket already warns about, in mirror image: it flags the stale-working-tree direction and was caught by its opposite.

Instrument validated before saying so: the file has no reference-style or HTML links, so the inline-link regex covers all 15; and injecting a deliberate broken link makes the resolver name that link.

## AC-3: there IS a real population — 7 links, none of them these

Swept all 140 markdown files under `learn/**` (109 filesystem links):

| file | dead target |
|---|---|
| `learn/benefits/body/JSONFirstUIs.md` | `../guides/fundamentals/AsymmetricUpdates.md` |
| `learn/benefits/body/ObjectPermanence.md` | `../guides/fundamentals/DeclarativeComponentTreesVsImperativeVdom.md` |
| `learn/blog/the-organism-already-existed.md` | `learn/guides/datahandling/DynamicGrids.md` |
| `learn/blog/the-organism-already-existed.md` | `learn/guides/advanced/CanvasArchitecture.md` |
| `learn/blog/v10-deep-dive-vdom-revolution.md` | `../../.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v10.3.0.md` |
| `learn/guides/fundamentals/ApplicationBootstrap.md` | `../benefits/body/OffTheMainThread.md` |
| `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/HtmlTemplatesUnderTheHood.md` | `../../../buildScripts/buildESModules.mjs` |

**These are relative-depth mistakes, not split fallout** — `../guides/…` where `../../guides/…` was meant, and repo-root paths written without a leading slash. Which makes the case for AC-4 *stronger*: the split is not the hazard, ordinary authoring is, and nothing catches it either way.

My first pass reported 17. Six of those were `/learn/comparisons/NeoVs*.md` root-absolute links my resolver joined relative to the referring file instead of the repo root, and three were portal dotted refs (`guides.events.DomEvents`) that are not filesystem paths at all. Both classes are instrument artifacts. Naming them because the checker in AC-4 has to get all three cases right or it will produce exactly this noise on every run.

Every repoint target verified present in the tracked tree first: a link that 404s somewhere
new is not an improvement. Two needed real answers rather than a depth fix — the release
notes moved to `resources/content/release-notes/` (no `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/` tree exists,
and `v10.3.0` has no GitHub release either, so a canonical URL would have 404'd too), and
the build script was renamed to `build/esmodules.mjs`, confirmed by finding the same
`processFileContent` import the prose describes. Its link TEXT named the old path, so both
moved.

The guard resolves against `git ls-files` — the index — not the filesystem. That is the
whole point: a checkout still carrying trees a merge removed reports every link healthy,
because the targets are sitting right there untracked. The index also includes staged
additions, so a PR may add a guide and link to it in one commit.

Three link classes, because two are not paths. A first pass over this repository produced 17
findings of which 7 were real: six were root-absolute links joined to the referrer's
directory instead of the repo root, and three were the portal's dotted addressing
(`guides.events.DomEvents`), which is not a filesystem path at all. Both are handled, and
skipped portal refs are counted in the output rather than silently dropped.

It reads reference-style and HTML links as well as inline ones, which is how the 8th finding
surfaced — `Speed.md`'s dead `<a href>` is invisible to an inline-only parser, and "no
findings" from a partial parser is indistinguishable from "no problems".

Wired into lint-staged on `learn/**/*.md` and a CI workflow triggered by `learn/**` plus the
guard's own files, so a checker that stops working is caught by the trigger that would have
caught the links.

```
  ✅ .github/STORY.md
  ✅ .github/VISION.md
  ✅ learn/benefits/ArchitectureOverview.md
  ✅ learn/benefits/body/ObjectPermanence.md
  ✅ learn/benefits/body/OffTheMainThread.md

  control  learn/benefits/DoesNotExist.md → correctly reports dead
```

**Five of five resolve. Zero dead links.** The control fires on a path that does not exist, so this is a measurement rather than an instrument that returns green at everything.

### Why the premise was wrong, and it is a reusable shape

The cut commit **repointed those 8 links to absolute URLs in the same commit that removed the trees**. The repointing and the removal were atomic, so nothing was ever orphaned.

⭐ **I reasoned that removing a tree must leave its inbound links dead. That is true in general and false here — because whoever executed the cut handled it.** I inferred the consequence of an action instead of measuring its result, and the inference was sound about mechanics and wrong about this repository.

### Disposition

- **AC-1 / AC-2:** already satisfied before this ticket was written. Not "fixed" — never broken.
- **The guard shipped anyway on a better argument**, and found a *different* **11** links: relative-depth authoring mistakes, not split fallout. That is the ticket's real subject and it is a genuine defect class.
- **Corrected text** — premise, AC disposition, Contract Ledger rows, the 11 actual repoints — is @neo-opus-ada's [comment 5464382349](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17809#issuecomment-5464382349), and it is the authoritative body from here.
- **PR #17859 may flip `Refs` → newline-isolated `Resolves #17809`.** Ruled.

**The ticket is not withdrawn**, because the delivered guard is real and needed. What changes is that it closes on *"relative links authored at the wrong depth"* rather than *"the split orphaned inbound links"* — a correct outcome reached from a wrong cause, which is worth recording as exactly that rather than quietly re-labelling.

**Process note, since the delay was mine:** the restatement sat from 19:24Z to 22:17Z waiting on a ruling only the ticket's author could give. @neo-opus-ada held the boundary correctly rather than editing a foreign-authored premise, and named the exit — *"if you would rather not spend the turn, `Refs` is the correct final state"* — so the PR was never actually blocked, only ambiguous. **Naming the state a non-answer resolves to is what kept this at hours instead of days.**

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

Refs #17809

* test(learn): a component-tier arm for link navigability (#17809)

The unit tier runs in Node with no DOM and no renderer, so it can prove a link
target exists in the git index but never that the rendered anchor carries a form
the router accepts. That gap shipped three unreachable links: they resolved on
disk, so a filesystem check reported them healthy while the portal returned 404.

This arm asserts on hrefs the real renderer produced in a real browser, and
classifies them against learn/tree.json - the same manifest the controller loads
- so the test and the app cannot disagree about what a reachable link is.

The dotted-id arm is deliberately inverted: it pins the ABSENCE of dotted-id
support, because getContentPath's replaceAll of dots for slashes is a no-op on
every current id and reads like support for both forms.

* feat(content): relative guide links become routes at render time (#17877)

learn/**/*.md has two consumers with incompatible link contracts. A GitHub
reader needs a filesystem-relative path; the portal needs #/learn/<id>, resolved
by an exact store.get against learn/tree.json. 112 of 137 learn files are
portal-served, so a relative .md href in one resolved against the document URL
and left the app entirely: ../benefits/ArchitectureOverview.md became
/apps/benefits/... and 404d.

Rewriting the ~78 relative links to routes would have fixed the portal and
broken GitHub. The links are correct as authored; the portal's translation of
them was missing, so the seam belongs in the renderer.

rewriteLinks joins the existing post-parse chain beside wrapMarkdownTables and
operates on marked's OUTPUT, which keeps marked the authority on what a link is.
Rewriting the markdown instead would re-decide that, and a second opinion
eventually disagrees with the renderer. The route is declared by the portal
view, not the generic src/ class, so every other markdown surface inherits an
identity no-op.

A target that climbs out of the content root is left untouched: popping an empty
segment list is silent, and unnoticed it yields a plausible id that resolves to
nothing.

The corpus went from 92 unreachable links to 0, with no allowlist. Repaired at
the source: 11 stale dotted hash routes, 6 root-absolute paths that were broken
on both surfaces, 2 HTML anchors, and 3 bare dotted tokens. Two pages that
served guides link to join tree.json beside their already-served siblings. Six
links into the repository tree are reported rather than absolved, since no
content route exists for source files.

check-whitespace gains --fix. Touching one line of a file that predates the hook
stages the whole file, turning historical trailing spaces into a blocker on an
unrelated change; 105 such lines sat in three of these guides. It strips only
what the check already rejects, and inherits both of its skips.

* fix(content): the router keeps a link's fragment, so the portal must split it (#17877)

Round-2 review found a false green and it reproduces. The route pattern
{*itemId} compiles to /^\/learn\/(.+)$/, so a deep link arrives as
`guides/x/Page#section` and the exact store lookup misses. The corpus oracle
stripped the fragment before checking and therefore certified a dead link. The
live corpus contains one: DockLayoutsAdoption.md#decision-3.

The split belongs to the app, not the shared router: route params are the
consuming app's to interpret, and widening the wildcard would change capture
semantics for every routed app.

Root-absolute targets no longer resolve from the repository root. Both readers
resolve them against an ORIGIN - a browser on GitHub sends /learn/x.md to
github.com/learn/x.md, and the portal sends it outside the app - so treating the
leading slash as "repo root" reported dead links as healthy. The first pass
over-corrected in the opposite direction, inventing six false positives by
joining them to the referrer; the honest answer is that there is no repository
path to check. Tightening it immediately surfaced a seventh live instance in
learn/blog that six manual repairs had missed.

learn/ now requires the unit suite. It is docs-only by path but not by
consequence: its links are checked against learn/tree.json, so a guide-only edit
can introduce a route resolving to no record, and the corpus gate was skipped on
exactly the PRs it exists to catch.

The check-whitespace --fix flag is reverted. It belongs to neither close target,
and it silently deleted a real Markdown hard break: Earthquakes.md:127 ends a
line whose successor is a continuation, so the two trailing spaces render a
line break. That break is restored explicitly as <br>, which survives a lint
that cannot tell semantics from accident.

* test(portal): an e2e arm that catches deleting the link rewrite (#17877)

The component and corpus arms proved properties of the rewrite in isolation, and
both stayed green when the production rewriteLinks invocation was deleted, because
neither executed it. Mutating the predicate is not mutating the feature.

This arm drives the real Portal, so the render path, the view's declared route,
the router and the tree store all participate. Both named mutations now red it:
removing the hook call, and removing the Portal's contentRoute.

A click arm was written and reverted. Its control - clicking the sidebar tree,
which owes nothing to this feature - failed in the same harness, and a red
assertion whose control is also red measures the harness rather than the subject.
Whether an in-content route link re-renders on click is therefore still open, and
is recorded as open rather than asserted either way.

* fix(test): the corpus sweep skipped every top-level learn guide (#17877)

git ls-files 'learn/**/*.md' does not match learn/*.md, so two served guides sat
outside the population while the run still reported clean. Surfaced by a reviewer
citing 114/137 nested against 116/140 including top-level: the count was not just
stale, the gap between the two numbers was the sweep's blind spot.

* fix(content): the link rewrite must see the quote styles the guard sees (#17877)

The build-time guard extracts raw-HTML anchors with `["']`; `rewriteLinks` matched
only `href="`. Two consumers of one corpus, two different predicates - so a
single-quoted relative link validates as healthy at build time and is then rendered
unrewritten, producing a href that works in a file tree and 404s in the SPA. That is
precisely the failure this pair exists to prevent, and it would be invisible.

Not hypothetical authoring: the corpus already carries two single-quoted anchors
(learn/guides/userinteraction/events/DomEvents.md:7 and :25). Both are absolute
https targets, so no link is broken today - the idiom is present, the relative case
has simply not been written yet.

The rewrite now mirrors HTML_HREF exactly and preserves the original quote
character, since normalising the delimiter would corrupt any attribute following it
on the same tag.

The corpus sweep's own oracle carried the same double-quote-only pattern, so it
would have skipped single-quoted anchors while reporting the population clean - a
third copy of the diverging predicate, in the instrument meant to detect it. Fixed,
and its capture group moved from 1 to 2 now that group 1 is the quote.

The sweep can only fail on links that exist today, so it cannot witness a quote
style the corpus has not yet used for a relative target. An explicit arm covers
both styles; reverting the regex to double-quote-only reds it.

* test(build): the guard's index-authority claim is witnessed, not asserted (#17809)

Every existing arm injects `tracked` and `read`, which proves the resolver and
nothing about where the CLI's inputs come from. The module header's central claim -
membership is the git index, so staged edits are scanned and a stale checkout's
untracked leftovers stay invisible - had no test at all. That claim is the entire
reason the guard resolves against git rather than the filesystem, and it was the one
thing not covered.

`trackedFiles` and the staged reader are now exported with an injectable root, so a
real repository can witness them. The reader is named `stagedReader` because what it
does is read `:path`, not open a file.

The new arms build a throwaway repo with a committed file, a staged-but-uncommitted

so index and worktree DIFFER. Without that divergence both readers return the same
bytes and the arm cannot tell them apart - it would pass against a filesystem
implementation. Pointing the reader at the worktree, or membership at `ls`, reds
them.

Also adds the single-quoted raw-HTML control the suite lacked. The guard already
handled both quote styles; nothing proved it, and the runtime rewriter had silently
diverged to double-quote-only (fixed in the preceding commit). Narrowing HTML_HREF
back to `"` reds the new arm.

* fix(links): guard and renderer share one predicate, and the portal fossil is gone (#17877)

Two divergences between the build-time guard and the runtime rewriter, both of which
certified something the other could not honour. They ship together because they are
one contract.

SCHEME AND CASE. URI schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 3986 3.1) and both readers
honour that, but both sides tested case-sensitively - and failed in OPPOSITE
directions on the same href. Given `HTTPS://example.com/docs/Foo.md`, rewriteLinks
did not skip it and rewrote a live absolute URL into `#/learn/...`, while the guard
classified it as a repository path and reported a live URL as a dead link.
`MailTo:a@b.c` classified as a portal ref. Both sides are now case-insensitive and
match ANY scheme rather than an enumerated list, which is what an absolute URI is.
The guard exports EXTERNAL_TARGET so the pair is pinned in one table; `src/` must not
import `buildScripts/`, so the duplication stays, but it is auditable now instead of
silent. `.md` is matched case-insensitively too.

Root-absolute is the one deliberate divergence and has its own arm: the renderer
leaves it alone (correct for a file-tree reader) while the guard REPORTS it, since
neither reader resolves a leading slash against the repository.

THE PORTAL FOSSIL. The guard resolved a portal ref by `id.replaceAll('.', '/') +
'.md'` and checking for that file. That rule described addressing the portal had
already left: 0 of 135 live tree.json ids contain a dot. So the guard certified
`benefits.body.ConfigSystem` as HEALTHY - a form dead in both readers, since the
router does an exact `store.get(itemId)` and no such file exists to open either. It
passed only by resolving onto a file a differently-spelled id owns. A guard that
blesses a known-dead syntax is fail-open for every future edit, which is the one
thing this guard exists not to be.

Portal refs are now judged by tree.json membership, which is the router's actual
predicate. That also fixes the other direction: `Benefits` and `GettingStarted` are
live ids for section nodes with NO markdown file, and any path-based rule reports
them dead. Restoring the dot-to-slash rule reds three arms, one per direction plus
the corpus arm.

A documented limit is pinned rather than left implied: live ids are slash-separated,
and a slash-separated target cannot be told from a relative path, so only the
slash-less form is ever classified `portal`.

The first version of the parity spec duplicated the renderer's regex as a local
helper and compared two literals both written in the test. It passed with the
production regex reverted to the buggy form, because it never touched production
code - the same mistake this PR was already corrected for once. It now drives the
real `rewriteLinks`; reverting the predicate reds 5 arms, each naming its href class.

* fix(build): the classifier was case-blind on suffixes, and the remedy text taught the fossil (#17809)

Two remnants of the same two clauses, both found by a reviewer reading the code
rather than the diff.

SUFFIX CASE. `FILE_SUFFIXES.some(value.endsWith)` was case-sensitive, so `Foo.MD`
classified as `portal` rather than `path` — a markdown file then judged against
tree.json membership and reported dead. Same class as the scheme fix in the previous
commit and it should have shipped with it: `Foo.MD` is one file on every system this
corpus is read on.

My own arm could not have caught it. It used `./Splitters.MD`, whose SLASH reaches
the path branch on `includes('/')` before the suffix test ever runs - it looks like a
case arm while witnessing nothing. The extension branch is only reachable for a bare
filename, so the new arms carry no slash.

REMEDY TEXT. Portal findings are unresolved by construction now, so the CLI's
`resolved === null` test described every dead dotted id as "is root-absolute", and
the footer instructed `learn/<dots-become-slashes>.md` - prescribing the exact rule
the previous commit retired. A dotted-id failure correctly reds, then tells the
author to restore the fossil that caused it.

Description now branches on KIND, and the footer states the real contract: ids match
learn/tree.json exactly, and relative .md links are rewritten for you. Extracted as
`describeFinding` so the prose is pinned by a spec instead of being reachable only by
running the binary - the guard's stated authority is part of what it must get right,
which is the whole reason this ticket exists.

Both mutants red only their own arm: case-sensitive suffix test reds the extension
arm, and collapsing the portal branch reds the remedy arm."
